items.stem: When is a single agent usually preferable to a multi-agent design?

options.text: When the task is cohesive and the overhead of coordination outweighs the benefit
options.rationale: Correct: multi-agent coordination adds cost and failure modes that a cohesive task does not need.

options.text: Always; multiple agents are never useful
options.rationale: Multi-agent designs do help for genuinely separable, parallel work.

options.text: Never; more agents are always better
options.rationale: More agents add coordination cost and new failure modes.

options.text: Only when the budget is unlimited
options.rationale: Budget alone does not decide topology.

items.explanation: Correct: multi-agent coordination adds cost and failure modes that a cohesive task does not need.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO keep a multi-agent system from looping or overspending? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A global step or token budget shared across agents
options.rationale: Correct: a shared budget caps total work regardless of which agent spends it.

options.text: An explicit termination condition the supervisor checks
options.rationale: Correct: a clear stop condition lets the system finish instead of looping.

options.text: Letting each agent decide its own unlimited budget
options.rationale: Unbounded per-agent budgets allow runaway cost.
Logging does not cause loops; removing it only hides them.

items.explanation: Correct: a shared budget caps total work regardless of which agent spends it.

items.stem: A worker agent keeps failing a delegated sub-task. What is the most likely design fix?

options.text: Give the worker a clearer sub-task contract with the context and success criteria it needs
options.rationale: Correct: vague delegation is a common cause; a precise contract fixes it.

options.text: Add ten more worker agents on the same vague task
options.rationale: More agents on a vague task reproduce the same failure.
Sampling temperature does not clarify a sub-task.
Removing logs hides the failure rather than fixing it.

items.explanation: Correct: vague delegation is a common cause; a precise contract fixes it.
